This approach leverages virtual collaboration tools, maintains team dynamics, and minimizes disruption to the project. It also accommodates the team member's relocation while allowing them to contribute to the project. Why the others are incorrect: A: Requiring all team members to be physically present may not be feasible or practical, especially when relocation is involved, and could negatively impact team morale. B: Offering an incentive may not guarantee the team member’s stay and does not address the long-term challenge of maintaining team collaboration after relocation. C: Replacing the team member disrupts team dynamics and progress, especially when the project is already 50% complete and the team member is critical to its success.

questions.q: A recently concluded quality audit failed and came back with multiple action items. A newly appointed project manager is reviewing the project status with the team. New stakeholders have been identified, and new audit resources may have to be added to the project. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Perform stakeholder engagement.
Perform integrated change control.
Update the quality management plan.
Update the risk management plan.

questions.e: Rationale: The failed quality audit and the need for new stakeholders and resources indicate potential changes to the project plan. The project manager should initiate the integrated change control process to evaluate the impact of these changes on the project’s scope, schedule, cost, and quality. This ensures that any adjustments are properly assessed, approved, and documented before implementation. Why the others are incorrect: A: While stakeholder engagement is important, it is not the immediate next step. Addressing the failed audit and resource requirements should take priority. C: Updating the quality management plan might be necessary later, but it should follow an integrated change control process to ensure proper evaluation and approval. D: Updating the risk management plan is important if new risks are identified, but it is not the immediate next step in addressing the audit findings and resource changes.

questions.q: A project requires the installation of a call center to support operations. It is estimated that the call center will need 100 people working on weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and weekends from 8:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Implement the call center with internal staff to ensure the work is performed according to the company's culture.
Work with 50% of the people internally and contract the other 50% to an outside company.
Delegate the analysis to the human resources (HR) department in order to organize the call center operations.
Conduct an alternative analysis to decide whether to hire people directly or contract with a company to do the job.

questions.e: Rationale: Before deciding how to staff the call center, the project manager should perform an alternative analysis. This involves evaluating the costs, benefits, risks, and feasibility of different options, such as hiring internal staff or outsourcing the work. This ensures that the chosen approach aligns with the project's goals, budget, and operational needs. Why the others are incorrect: A: Implementing the call center with internal staff without evaluating alternatives may not be the most cost-effective or feasible solution. B: Splitting the staffing between internal and external resources is a possible outcome but should be determined after conducting an alternative analysis. C: Delegating the analysis to HR without involving the project manager in decision-making might not align with project requirements or priorities.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a project to develop accounting software for a trading firm. As the outcomes are being delivered, a new risk is identified regarding an indirect tax regulation that is being changed by the government in the next 6 months. This risk will have a significant impact on the project outcomes. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Determine the impact of the risk and prioritize outcomes that do not affect the tax module.
Delay developing the indirect tax module until the tax regulation comes into effect.
Assess the impact of the risk with an expert and prioritize further outcomes with the client.
Analyze the impact of the risk and discuss with the team to determine how to separate the tax module.

questions.e: Rationale: When a new risk is identified, particularly one with significant potential impact, the project manager should involve an expert to assess the risk’s implications thoroughly. Collaborating with the client ensures that the project outcomes align with their priorities, considering the identified risk. This approach enables informed decision-making and appropriate adjustments to the project plan. Why the others are incorrect: A: Prioritizing outcomes that do not affect the tax module without a proper assessment might lead to suboptimal decision-making and misalignment with client expectations. B: Delaying the tax module development could impact the project timeline and delivery if not agreed upon with the client. D: Discussing with the team to determine how to separate the tax module without first involving experts or clients may overlook critical details and priorities.

questions.q: A project manager has recently moved to an organization to lead a key project. The project manager notices that team performance is below the target, and the tasks assigned are not delivered on time. Team commitment is also not as appropriate as it should be. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Study and determine the appropriate leadership style suitable for the team.
Hire a project team leader who can influence the project team members.
Schedule a meeting and communicate the performance concern to the team.
Apply an agile approach to help improve team performance.

questions.e: Rationale: Every team has unique dynamics and challenges, and a project manager’s leadership style plays a crucial role in addressing performance issues and motivating the team. By analyzing the team’s needs and selecting a leadership style that fosters collaboration, accountability, and engagement, the project manager can improve team performance and commitment effectively. Why the others are incorrect: B: Hiring a project team leader may not address the root cause of the issue and could delay progress further. C: Communicating performance concerns without understanding the underlying issues or adapting the leadership approach may demoralize the team. D: Applying an Agile approach may be helpful in some cases, but it may not be appropriate or feasible for all projects or organizations without first addressing the leadership and team dynamics.

questions.q: Due to unforeseen circumstances, a contractor was unable to mobilize the project team, which was necessary to conduct face-to-face meetings and discussions. Virtual meetings were subsequently put in place, but the local project team and end users now face a communication gap that is causing the team's low performance. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the contractor to solve this problem because this is a contractual obligation.
Terminate the contract and initiate a new one with a local contractor.
Implement key performance indicators (KPIs) and convince the contractor to engage the team.
Reassess continually to remove blockers for the team.

questions.e: Rationale: When virtual meetings lead to communication gaps and low team performance, the project manager should continually reassess the situation to identify and remove blockers hindering effective collaboration. This proactive approach ensures that the team has the resources, tools, and processes necessary to overcome challenges, even in a virtual environment. Why the others are incorrect: A: Asking the contractor to solve the problem solely shifts responsibility without addressing the immediate communication issues affecting team performance. B: Terminating the contract is an extreme response that could lead to delays and increased costs, and should only be considered as a last resort after all other options are explored. C: Implementing KPIs and engaging the contractor may provide clarity on performance metrics, but it does not directly address the communication gaps affecting team collaboration.

questions.q: As a result of the first iteration review, the stakeholders' feedback indicated that they saw more technical features than business ones. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Include this topic in the next iteration retrospective.
Review this topic with the product owner before the next iteration planning.
Discuss this topic with the team in the next daily meeting.
Ask the product owner to review this topic in the next iteration planning.

questions.e: Rationale: The product owner is responsible for prioritizing the product backlog and ensuring that the deliverables align with business needs and stakeholder expectations. By reviewing the feedback with the product owner before the next iteration planning, the project manager can help ensure that business-oriented features are prioritized in the upcoming iterations. Why the others are incorrect: A: Including this topic in the next retrospective focuses on improving team processes but does not directly address stakeholder concerns about feature prioritization. C: Discussing this topic in the next daily meeting does not address the backlog prioritization, which is the product owner's responsibility. D: Asking the product owner to review the topic in the next iteration planning may delay addressing the feedback and does not ensure proactive collaboration before planning.

questions.q: A project manager just completed a successful deployment and is preparing to transition the project to an operational state before starting closeout actions. What should the project manager do to ensure that the project is ready to move to an operational state? *

o.t: Meet with the project team to review the work breakdown structure (WBS) and confirm deliverables have been delivered.
Develop a plan to repay the technical debt incurred during the project and ensure that the project sponsor agrees with the plan.
Review the project approval requirements in the project charter and confirm who will be approving the project.
Refer to the project's work in progress (WIP) reports to ensure that there is no additional work in the backlog.

questions.e: Rationale: Before transitioning a project to an operational state, the project manager must ensure that the project meets the approval requirements specified in the project charter. This includes confirming who is responsible for approving the transition and verifying that all criteria have been met. This step ensures alignment with the project’s objectives and formalizes the transition to operations. Why the others are incorrect: A: While reviewing the WBS can help confirm deliverables, it does not address the formal approval process required for transitioning to operations. B: Addressing technical debt is important, but it is typically part of ongoing operations or follow-up projects, not a prerequisite for transitioning the project. D: Reviewing WIP reports ensures there is no additional work pending, but it does not confirm readiness for the operational transition or meet the formal approval criteria.

questions.q: A project manager has been assigned to a hybrid project that must receive approval from a government regulator. During the daily standups, one member reported an impediment that requires collaboration from an expert who is assigned to another project. What should the project manager do first in this situation? *

o.t: Review the project's key performance indicators (KPIs) to determine the impact of this assignment.
Check the expert's availability within the organization on an as-needed basis.
Develop the team member's capacities through mentoring and training.
Ask the project sponsor to assign a new resource with the necessary expertise to the team.

questions.e: Rationale: When an impediment arises that requires collaboration from an expert assigned to another project, the project manager’s first step should be to check the expert’s availability. This ensures the resource can be engaged as needed without disrupting other projects. Efficient resource coordination is critical in hybrid projects where expertise is vital for resolving issues and maintaining progress. Why the others are incorrect: A: Reviewing KPIs does not directly address the immediate need to resolve the impediment caused by the lack of expert availability. C: Mentoring and training the team member may take too long to address the current impediment and might not provide the required expertise. D: Requesting the sponsor to assign a new resource is a reactive step that should only be considered if the required expert is completely unavailable or the organization lacks the needed expertise.

questions.q: Travel restrictions are suddenly imposed during a project's execution. The team members reside in different geographic locations. What should the project manager do next to address this issue? *

o.t: Halt all processes until procurement and implementation of solutions are completed.
Place a hold on activities until the team can resume the work on-site.
Ask the team members to proceed independently while examining needs and alternatives.
Obtain and implement the sponsor's recommendations for a solution.

questions.e: Rationale: When travel restrictions are imposed, the project manager should ensure that the team continues to work independently on tasks that do not require on-site collaboration. Simultaneously, the project manager should evaluate alternative solutions, such as virtual collaboration tools or adjusted processes, to minimize disruptions and maintain progress. Why the others are incorrect: A: Halting all processes is unnecessarily disruptive and may lead to significant delays, especially when alternatives could be explored. B: Placing activities on hold delays the project unnecessarily and does not address the need to adapt to the new circumstances. D: While the sponsor’s input is valuable, relying solely on the sponsor for a solution might delay action and prevent the team from continuing progress on tasks that can be done remotely.

questions.q: A project manager works in a startup company and is in charge of a key project that has critical and time-sensitive delivery objectives. One of the project team members missed completing an assigned deliverable on time, despite repeated assurances from the team member that it would be completed on time. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Record the issue then refocus the team's efforts on delivering the next set of deliverables.
Give the team member a formal warning for the negative impact due to failure to deliver and not meet deadlines.
Hold a team meeting to discuss team member commitments and communications.
Meet with the team member and work on a development plan for them to avoid missed deliverables in the future.

questions.e: Rationale: The project manager should address the issue directly with the team member to understand the reasons for the missed deliverable and collaboratively create a development plan to improve their performance. This approach ensures accountability while fostering professional growth, reducing the likelihood of similar issues in the future. It aligns with effective leadership and team development practices. Why the others are incorrect: A: Simply recording the issue and refocusing on the next deliverables ignores the underlying problem and risks recurring issues. B: Giving a formal warning may harm morale and trust, especially without first understanding the root cause of the missed deliverable. C: While discussing team commitments in a meeting can be valuable, it may not address the specific performance issue with the individual team member effectively.

questions.q: A technology project is delivering new functionality on a new platform. Several team resources are starting to train their teams, but they are asking questions about the training that the project will provide. What should the project manager's first action be? *

o.t: Indicate that on the new technology is the functional manager's responsibility.
Review the project charter to determine if the training is in scope and, if not, put in a change request.
Consult with the organizational change management specialist as to what the training plan includes.
Document the skill requirements for the product to determine what training is needed.

questions.e: Rationale: The project manager’s first action should be to consult with the organizational change management specialist to understand the existing training plan and its scope. This ensures that the project aligns with organizational strategies for change and that the necessary training is provided to ensure successful adoption of the new functionality. Why the others are incorrect: A: Delegating the responsibility to the functional manager without assessing the scope of training in the project may lead to confusion and mismanagement. B: Reviewing the project charter is important but secondary. Consulting with the change management specialist provides clarity on whether training is already planned and its details. D: Documenting skill requirements is useful for planning training but should come after understanding what the current training plan includes.

questions.q: At the end of a canceled project, the project manager sent surveys to all stakeholders. The survey also included templates for stakeholders to outline situations, solutions, results and suggestions. How should the project manager use the information collected? *

o.t: Map the lessons learned against work breakdown structure (WBS) components.
Archive the survey responses with project artifacts for future projects.
Use the information to restart the project.
Evaluate the information collected on areas of improvement.

questions.e: Rationale: The primary purpose of collecting survey responses and stakeholder input is to evaluate areas of improvement for future projects. By analyzing the feedback, the project manager can identify lessons learned, improve processes, and implement best practices to enhance future project performance and stakeholder satisfaction. Why the others are incorrect: A: Mapping lessons learned to the work breakdown structure (WBS) components may help categorize the lessons, but it is not the primary use of survey feedback. B: Archiving the responses is necessary for documentation purposes, but it does not involve actively using the feedback to drive improvements. C: Using the information to restart the project assumes that restarting is feasible and in scope, which is not indicated in the question.

questions.q: During the last two iterations of a project, one of the team members had low performance. The project manager conducted two feedback sessions with the team member and escalated the issue to the resource manager and project sponsor, but there has been no improvement. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Escalate the situation again to the project sponsor.
Review this obstacle during the daily standup meeting.
Request a new resource to execute the activities.
Provide feedback to the resource at the sprint review.

questions.e: Rationale: When a team member's performance does not improve despite feedback sessions and escalation to the resource manager and project sponsor, it indicates that the situation is affecting the project's progress. The next step is to request a replacement resource to ensure the project's activities are completed as planned. This minimizes disruption and maintains the team's productivity. Why the others are incorrect: A: Escalating again to the sponsor is unlikely to yield different results, as previous escalations have already been ineffective. B: Discussing the obstacle during the daily standup meeting may waste time and could demoralize the team without resolving the core issue. D: Providing feedback during the sprint review is too late to address the immediate issue and may not resolve the ongoing performance problem.

questions.q: During the execution of a project to develop a prototype, the customer asks the project manager to stop the prototype line and purge a specific component based on recent reliability tests that have deemed the component to be deficient. The project manager checked the quality management plan and there is no reference to this component. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Inform the project sponsor of the situation and wait for the sponsor to provide further directions.
Call a technical meeting with the customer to agree on a specification for the component and document it in the quality management plan.
Submit a change request to proceed with the replacement of the component and wait for further customer instructions.
Keep running the manufacturing line because there are no quality specifications for this component.

questions.e: Rationale: Since the customer has requested a change based on new reliability test results, the project manager should follow the change control process by submitting a change request. This ensures the request is formally documented, reviewed, and approved before implementation. This approach aligns with proper project governance and ensures the customer’s concerns are addressed while maintaining control over project scope and quality. Why the others are incorrect: A: Informing the sponsor without taking any action delays resolution and does not follow the formal change management process. B: While discussing specifications with the customer can help clarify requirements, it should be part of the change control process rather than bypassing it. D: Continuing the manufacturing line without addressing the customer’s concerns could lead to wasted resources, reputational damage, and customer dissatisfaction.

questions.q: An organization is undergoing an agile transformation. The executive leadership team is concerned that they will lose control over the scope of the project. What should the project manager, who is responsible for this project, do to mitigate this risk? *

o.t: Ensure that the executive leadership team approves all scope that is being proposed by the multiple agile teams to avoid misalignment.
Propose a governance model that empowers the teams while providing the necessary oversight to the executive leadership team.
Propose a multilayered gate system based on risks and financial expenditures, involving the executive leadership team as needed.
Assure the executive leadership team that the current governance model will not be affected by the agile approach.

questions.e: Rationale: An agile transformation requires a balance between empowering teams to make decisions and providing the necessary oversight to ensure alignment with organizational goals. Proposing a governance model that addresses both aspects mitigates the leadership team’s concerns about losing control while maintaining the flexibility and adaptability of agile practices. This approach fosters trust and ensures a collaborative transformation. Why the others are incorrect: A: Requiring the executive leadership team to approve all proposed scope undermines the autonomy of agile teams and may create bottlenecks, reducing agility. C: A multilayered gate system adds unnecessary complexity and slows down the decision-making process, contradicting agile principles. D: Simply assuring the leadership team that the current governance model will remain intact overlooks the need for adjustments to governance that align with agile practices.

questions.q: A project manager has been hired to help coordinate an ongoing project. Historically the biggest problem as reported by the company's CEO is that the change request process has been handled by managers who did not have clear information on the project schedule and budget. This information has been inconsistent and handled by finance, risk and functional subject matter experts (SMEs). What should the project manager do to control this situation? *

o.t: Redefine the communications management plan.
Develop an integrated change management plan.
Document the risk in the project risk register.
Review the scope defined in the project charter.

questions.e: Rationale: The issue described highlights a lack of coordination and clarity in the change management process, particularly in terms of the impact on schedule and budget. Developing an integrated change management plan ensures that all change requests are systematically evaluated, tracked, and approved with accurate and consistent information. This plan aligns the efforts of all stakeholders (e.g., finance, risk, and SMEs) and provides a structured approach to managing changes effectively. Why the others are incorrect: A: While redefining the communications management plan may help improve information sharing, it does not directly address the core issue of inconsistent handling of change requests. C: Documenting the risk in the risk register acknowledges the issue but does not actively resolve it or improve the change management process. D: Reviewing the scope in the project charter is valuable but does not address the need for a clear and consistent change management process.

questions.q: A self-organizing team for a critical project is consistently delivering value according to their commitments. During a retrospective, the project manager observed that most of the team members were stressed due to over commitments. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Help the team members by organizing regular stress-relieving and team- building sessions.
Request additional resources to continue delivering value while reducing team stress.
Support the team during the planning phase to only commit to what they are able to deliver.
Ask individual team members to plan staggered leave to avoid becoming stressed.

questions.e: Rationale: The root cause of the team's stress is overcommitment. The project manager should support the team in the planning phase by helping them realistically assess their capacity and commit only to deliverables they can achieve within their available resources and time. This ensures sustainable performance and reduces the risk of burnout while maintaining value delivery. Why the others are incorrect: A: Stress-relieving and team-building sessions may help temporarily alleviate stress but do not address the underlying issue of overcommitment. B: Requesting additional resources may not be feasible or necessary if the issue can be resolved by better planning and realistic commitments. D: Staggered leave planning is important for overall work-life balance but does not directly address the stress caused by overcommitment.

questions.q: In an iteration-based marketing project, a product is scheduled to be launched at the sixth iteration. In the third iteration demo, the marketing team expressed that they need five iterations to launch the product and they have not started yet. What should the project team have done to avoid this issue? *

o.t: Held a touchpoint with marketing before the demo to discuss any impediments
Scheduled a demo presentation of the product during the first reason
Asked the marketing team to start working on the product immediately
Confirmed marketing requirements and constraints when adding to the backlog

questions.e: Rationale: To avoid this issue, the project team should have confirmed the marketing requirements and constraints when adding work items to the product backlog. This ensures that dependencies, such as the time needed by the marketing team for product launch preparation, are identified and accounted for during planning. Proper communication and alignment early in the project help avoid surprises later. Why the others are incorrect: A: Holding a touchpoint before the demo would help address current impediments but does not resolve the issue of missing early alignment on requirements and constraints. B: Scheduling a demo in the first iteration might provide earlier feedback but does not address the need to confirm marketing requirements and timelines in advance. C: Asking the marketing team to start immediately assumes they can do so without proper planning or preparation, which may not be feasible.

questions.q: A project manager leads a development project for a mobile chatting application. One of the experienced developers constantly creates conflicts with the other team members. As a result, the other team members are refusing to work with the developer. Since the developer is a high performer, the project goals may be negatively impacted if they leave the team. What should the project manager do in this situation? *

o.t: Meet with the developer and ask them to be respectful with the other team members and work together as a team.
Meet with the team members and developer individually to understand the situation and build an action plan accordingly.
Collect the team's feedback and send it to human resources (HR) to resolve the conflict.
Arrange a team-building training session and require all of the team members to attend.

questions.e: Rationale: To effectively resolve the conflict, the project manager should first meet with all parties involved individually to understand the root cause of the issue. This helps ensure that all perspectives are considered and an informed action plan can be developed to address the situation constructively. The approach fosters mutual respect and teamwork while retaining the high-performing developer. Why the others are incorrect: A: Asking the developer to be respectful without understanding the situation may oversimplify the issue and fail to address the root cause of the conflict. C: Escalating to HR without first attempting to resolve the issue at the team level may create unnecessary tension and harm team morale. D: While team-building training can help improve collaboration, it is not sufficient to resolve a specific conflict without first understanding its cause.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a project that is in the execution phase. Due to a company reorganization, some key project team members are likely to leave the project. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Discuss this issue with the affected team members and support them during the transition.
Start looking for replacements as soon as possible to help prevent any schedule slippage.
Engage with the project sponsor to ensure that this change does not affect the project execution.
Determine the impact to the project and implement mitigations per the project management plan.

questions.e: Rationale: When key team members are likely to leave the project, the project manager should first evaluate the impact on the project in terms of scope, schedule, cost, and quality. Based on this assessment, the project manager can implement mitigations as outlined in the project management plan, such as reallocating resources, adjusting timelines, or onboarding replacements, to minimize disruptions to project execution. Why the others are incorrect: A: Supporting the team members during their transition is important but does not address the project's impact or mitigation needs. B: Starting the search for replacements is a potential mitigation action but should come after assessing the project’s impact and following the project management plan. C: Engaging with the sponsor is useful for escalations or support but is not the immediate next step. The project manager must first assess and mitigate the impact.

questions.q: Some of the more experienced members of a project team have complained about the project manager. The senior project team members feel that the project manager is micromanaging them and preventing them from completing their work. What should the project manager do when made aware of these issues? *

o.t: Set up a team building event to bring synergy back to the project team.
Adjust the project manager's management style to better fit senior team members.
Ask for advice on how to be a better mentor to these team members.
Meet daily with each senior team member to monitor project status.

questions.e: Rationale: Experienced team members typically prefer autonomy in their work and may feel frustrated by micromanagement. The project manager should adapt their management style to provide these team members with the independence they need, focusing on enabling and supporting rather than controlling. This approach fosters trust, improves morale, and enhances productivity. Why the others are incorrect: A: A team-building event can help improve team cohesion but does not address the specific issue of micromanagement. C: Seeking mentorship advice is valuable for personal development but does not directly resolve the immediate concern of the team members. D: Meeting daily with senior team members to monitor project status could exacerbate the issue of micromanagement and further strain relationships.

questions.q: A new building project is in the middle of its life cycle. The municipality informs the project manager that due to new regulations, the parking lot around the project has to accommodate twice the number of cars than was initially planned. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Request the project sponsor to fund this change as it is a new regulation, then order the materials in order to start working.
Assess the impact of the required change and consult with the executive sponsors to determine the best course of action.
Ask the designers to start designing a solution for this new requirement while the project is running and determine the funding for this change.
Have the company's lawyers write to the municipality and reject the change as it was not part of the scope approved by the municipality.

questions.e: Rationale: When faced with a new regulation that impacts the project, the project manager should first assess the impact of the change on the project’s scope, schedule, cost, and resources. After understanding the implications, the project manager should engage the executive sponsors to discuss and determine the best course of action, ensuring that the project complies with the regulation while managing stakeholder expectations. Why the others are incorrect: A: Ordering materials and committing resources without first assessing the impact and gaining sponsor approval is premature and may lead to inefficiencies or misalignment with project goals. C: Starting design work immediately assumes the change will be implemented without fully understanding its impact or securing approval, which could result in wasted effort or rework. D: Rejecting the change outright without exploring its implications is not a viable option when the change is due to a new regulation that must be complied with.

questions.q: A project manager is asked to develop maintenance planning software for a power plant. A similar project was executed by another department in the organization that was later closed due to low performance. The project manager is concerned about the project's performance and wants to take action in advance to ensure the project success. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Evaluate the project risk and add external experts to address the potential risks.
Inform the project sponsor about the risk and try to convince them to withdraw from the project.
Continue executing the project as planned and add more resources if they are required.
Review the lessons learned on similar projects so that they do not fall back into the same pattern.

questions.e: Rationale: Reviewing the lessons learned from similar projects is a proactive way to identify potential pitfalls and avoid repeating mistakes. This allows the project manager to incorporate best practices and address known challenges early in the project, increasing the likelihood of success. Why the others are incorrect: A: Adding external experts may address some risks but does not tackle the root causes identified in the lessons learned from the previous project. B: Informing the sponsor and suggesting withdrawal is unnecessarily drastic and ignores opportunities to mitigate risks and improve performance. C: Continuing the project as planned without addressing known issues from similar projects could lead to repeating the same mistakes, even with additional resources.

questions.q: A team shared a complaint regarding the scrum master during the last sprint review. The team expressed that they were delayed because the scrum master did not remove impediments, such as scheduling some meetings with external teams and obtaining a room to work collaboratively, among other critical blockers. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Request an additional resource to assist in solving all of the impediments listed by the team.
Determine and agree when a situation becomes an impediment to be solved by the scrum master.
Request the team review and prioritize the open impediments to resolve all of them as soon as possible.
Push back, explaining that a self-organized team should address all of the problems to get the work done.

questions.e: Rationale: The scrum master’s role includes removing impediments that block the team from progressing. By determining and agreeing with the team on what constitutes an impediment, the project manager can ensure clarity on roles and responsibilities. This approach fosters accountability, avoids misunderstandings, and improves collaboration between the scrum master and the team. Why the others are incorrect: A: Adding additional resources might address the immediate issues, but it does not solve the root cause of the scrum master not effectively managing impediments. C: Prioritizing and resolving impediments is important, but the team relies on the scrum master to address critical blockers. This option overlooks the scrum master’s responsibility. D: While a self-organized team addresses many issues themselves, the scrum master is specifically responsible for removing impediments that are outside the team's control.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a project that involves on-site and remote team members. One task that was assigned to a team member in another country appears to be behind schedule. When the project manager inquires about this, the team member claims that the task was completed and that this was reported to the team lead via a telephone conversation. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Communicate the ground rules, principles and reporting methods to the project stakeholders
Penalize the project team lead for not updating the project documentation properly.
Review this issue with the team lead for possible ways to resolve this situation
Issue guidance to the team member about reporting directly to the project manager

questions.e: Rationale: The project manager should ensure that all team members, including leads and remote contributors, understand and follow the established ground rules, reporting principles, and methods. This ensures consistent communication, avoids misunderstandings, and maintains accountability. Reinforcing these rules will help prevent similar issues in the future. Why the others are incorrect: B: Penalizing the team lead does not address the root cause of the issue and may harm team morale. C: Reviewing the issue with the team lead may provide insight but does not ensure that the reporting process is clearly communicated and followed. D: Directing the team member to report only to the project manager bypasses the team structure and could lead to confusion and inefficiencies.

questions.q: A project engineer in country A is complaining about the sample received from the supplier in country B because the sample is not the correct length. During a telephone conference, the supplier checked the drawings and insisted that the measurement was accurate. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Escalate the issue to the purchasing department for review.
Evaluate the procurement contract to determine the agreed-upon specifications.
Hire a company in country B to perform a quality check before shipment.
Add an additional task to cut the received part according to the specifications.

questions.e: Rationale: The project manager should first refer to the procurement contract to verify the agreed-upon specifications for the part. This ensures that any disagreements about the sample's measurements are based on documented requirements. This step establishes clarity, helps resolve the issue objectively, and determines whether the supplier has met the contractual obligations. Why the others are incorrect: A: Escalating the issue to the purchasing department may involve additional stakeholders, but the project manager should first confirm whether the supplier has adhered to the agreed specifications. C: Hiring a third party to perform a quality check might help in the future but is unnecessary at this stage until the contractual specifications are verified. D: Adding a task to cut the part to specifications is a workaround that might incur additional costs and effort without resolving the underlying issue.

questions.q: The project manager is having difficulty communicating with one of the team members. The team member recently attended a training course and has been training other team members in a new agile technique. However sometimes the team member is forceful in pushing ideas even if other team members are uncomfortable. What personality indicators should the project manager consider when determining what communication style to use with this team member? *

o.t: Extroverted and Judging
Extroverted and Perceiving
Introverted and Judging
Introverted and Perceiving

questions.e: Rationale: The behavior described—forcefully pushing ideas and taking charge—suggests that the team member may have an extroverted personality, meaning they are outgoing, assertive, and energized by interactions. The judging trait indicates a preference for structure, decision-making, and a clear plan, which aligns with the team member's inclination to strongly advocate for their ideas, even at the expense of team comfort. Understanding this personality type can help the project manager adapt their communication style to be more collaborative, structured, and inclusive. Why the others are incorrect: B. Extroverted and Perceiving: While this combination is also outgoing, perceiving individuals prefer flexibility and openness to new ideas, which does not align with the forceful behavior described. C. Introverted and Judging: Introverted individuals are more reserved and less likely to forcefully push their ideas in group settings. D. Introverted and Perceiving: This combination describes someone who is quiet and adaptable, which is inconsistent with the assertiveness described.

questions.q: A project manager is working on a project with multiple workstreams. One of the workstreams missed its deadline multiple times. Who should the project manager speak to about this situation to ensure it does not happen again? *

o.t: Workstream leader and project sponsor
Workstream leader alone
Workstream leader and functional manager
Workstream leader and project management office (PMO)

questions.e: According to the PMBOK Guide, a workstream is a logical grouping of project activities that produces a specific deliverable or sub-deliverable within a project. A workstream leader is the person who is responsible for planning, executing, monitoring, and controlling the workstream activities and deliverables. A functional manager is the person who has management authority over an organizational unit, such as a department, within a functional organization1. In this scenario, the project manager faces a situation where one of the workstreams has missed its deadline multiple times, affecting the project schedule and performance. The project manager should speak to the workstream leader and the functional manager about this situation to ensure it does not happen again. The project manager should communicate with the workstream leader to understand the root causes of the delays, identify the risks and issues, and agree on the corrective and preventive actions. The project manager should also communicate with the functional manager to obtain the necessary resources, support, and guidance for the workstream leader and the workstream team. The project manager should facilitate the collaboration and coordination between the workstream leader and the functional manager to ensure the alignment of expectations, objectives, and deliverables1. The other options are not as suitable as option C. Option A involves speaking to the workstream leader and the project sponsor. The project sponsor is the person or group who provides resources and support for the project and is accountable for enabling success1. However, the project sponsor is not directly involved in the management or execution of the workstream activities and deliverables. The project sponsor may not have the detailed knowledge or authority to address the specific issues or challenges faced by the workstream leader and the workstream team. Option B involves speaking to the workstream leader alone. This option may not be sufficient to resolve the situation, as the workstream leader may need the support and assistance of other managers or stakeholders to overcome the delays and improve the workstream performance. Option D involves speaking to the workstream leader and the project management office (PMO). The PMO is an organizational structure that standardizes the project-related governance processes and facilitates the sharing of resources, methodologies, tools, and techniques1. However, the PMO may not have the direct responsibility or authority over the workstream activities and deliverables. The PMO may not be able to provide the specific resources, support, or guidance needed by the workstream leader and the workstream team1. References: 1: Project Management Institute. (2023). A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide) - Seventh Edition. Newtown Square, PA: Author.

questions.q: A project team has been formed and the tasks have been assigned to each team member. All team members have agreed to follow a hybrid project approach. What should the project manager do to ensure the team performs as an organized unit? *

o.t: Advise the team to adjust their work habits and behaviors to allow for better conflict resolution
Call a team meeting to discuss team members' strengths and weaknesses
Establish rules and regulations for team members with consequences if the goals are not reached
Establish team behavior and develop an understating of how to work together

questions.e: Rationale: In a hybrid project approach, team members must work collaboratively and adapt to varying situations. To ensure the team functions as an organized unit, it is crucial to define how the team will work together. This involves establishing shared norms, roles, and behaviors that promote cooperation and collaboration, and aligning expectations for team dynamics. Why not the other options? A. Advise the team to adjust their work habits and behaviors to allow for better conflict resolution: This focuses on conflict resolution only, which is a reactive measure. The project manager should be proactive by setting up team norms to avoid conflicts in the first place. B. Call a team meeting to discuss team members' strengths and weaknesses: While understanding strengths and weaknesses is helpful, it does not directly ensure the team works as an organized unit. C. Establish rules and regulations for team members with consequences if the goals are not reached: This approach is overly rigid and punitive, which can negatively affect team morale and productivity.

questions.q: A project manager finds an unexpected issue halfway through a customer's protect. After analysis, the project team determines that the issue will affect the timeline unless more resources are allocated to the project. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Meet with the project team to discuss internally whether they think cost is more important to the customer than the timeline
Adjust the timeline since in the past the customer would not pay any additional costs then inform the customer of the change
Inform the customer of the issue and discuss the options so that they are able to make a decision on cost versus timeline
Absorb the additional cost for the additional resources internally so that the project completes within the timeline

questions.e: Rationale: When an unexpected issue arises that impacts a project, the project manager must communicate openly with the customer. In this scenario, the issue has implications for both cost and timeline. It is critical to involve the customer in the decision-making process, providing them with the necessary information to choose between allocating additional resources (which increases costs) or accepting a timeline adjustment. Why not the other options? A. Meet with the project team to discuss internally whether they think cost is more important to the customer than the timeline: Assuming what the customer values without consulting them directly is inappropriate and can lead to dissatisfaction. B. Adjust the timeline since in the past the customer would not pay any additional costs then inform the customer of the change: This assumes past behavior dictates current decisions, which is not professional or aligned with proper stakeholder engagement. D. Absorb the additional cost for the additional resources internally so that the project completes within the timeline: This is not a sustainable approach. The project manager does not have the authority to make such a decision without evaluating the project's budget constraints and getting the necessary approvals.

questions.q: A newly formed project team includes team members who have been working in the company for a long time as well as team members who are new to the company. The project team members discovered that there is a gap in communication between these two groups, and they are finding it hard to collaborate with one another. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the experienced members to lead the junior members to facilitate skill transfer.
Encourage team members to focus on delivering results with their specialized skills.
Organize networking sessions to allow the team members to get to know one another.
Ask the team to self-organize and escalate any issues to the project manager.

questions.e: Rationale: Building a cohesive team is critical for project success, especially when there are communication gaps. Organizing networking sessions provides an opportunity for team members to bond, understand each other better, and build trust. This is a proactive approach to fostering collaboration and addressing the communication challenges between experienced and new members. Why not the other options? A. Ask the experienced members to lead the junior members to facilitate skill transfer: While skill transfer is valuable, it does not directly address the communication gap or build mutual respect and collaboration between the two groups. B. Encourage team members to focus on delivering results with their specialized skills: This is a task-focused approach that does not address the root cause of the communication issue, which could impact overall project efficiency. D. Ask the team to self-organize and escalate any issues to the project manager: Leaving the team to resolve communication issues without guidance may worsen the problem and delay the resolution. The project manager needs to take an active role in team building.

questions.q: A project manager who recently joined the company has been assigned to manage a software project for a major recurring customer. What should the project manager do to enhance the budget estimations for the project? *

o.t: Discuss the budget with the team during the daily standups to ensure the budget is under control.
Review budget-related lessons learned from similar projects.
Invite the client to the kick-off meeting and create the project budget during the meeting.
Implement an agile approach to avoid using a fixed budget.

questions.e: Rationale: To enhance budget estimations, reviewing lessons learned from similar projects is a best practice. This approach provides insights into previous successes, challenges, and actual versus estimated costs, allowing the project manager to make more accurate and informed budget predictions. Leveraging historical data is a key tool in project management. Why not the other options? A. Discuss the budget with the team during the daily standups to ensure the budget is under control: Daily standups are typically focused on tasks and progress, not detailed budget discussions. Budget control is a broader responsibility that requires specific planning and monitoring activities. C. Invite the client to the kick-off meeting and create the project budget during the meeting: While involving the client in discussions is essential, the project budget should not be created during the kick-off meeting. Budget creation requires detailed analysis and preparation beforehand. D. Implement an agile approach to avoid using a fixed budget: Agile approaches may provide flexibility, but most projects, including those for major recurring customers, still require budget estimations upfront to align with business goals and expectations.

questions.q: A multimillion-dollar project has started and is in the execution phase. A local regulatory authority has just announced changes to the requirements that will need to be implemented in 6 months, prior to completing the project execution phase. What should the project manager do next? *

o.t: Add the new requirements to the project scope immediately since they are mandatory changes.
Review the new requirements with the compliance department to determine if a change request is needed.
Ignore the new requirements as the current budget and schedule do not allow for any changes.
Proceed with the defined project requirements and delay implementing the new requirements.

questions.e: Rationale: When a regulatory authority announces new requirements, it is important to assess the impact on the project. The project manager should first consult with the compliance department to confirm whether the changes are mandatory and to understand their implications. If the changes are confirmed as necessary, a formal change request must be submitted to evaluate the impact on scope, budget, and schedule, and then incorporated into the project plan. Why not the other options? A. Add the new requirements to the project scope immediately since they are mandatory changes: While regulatory changes may be mandatory, the project manager must still follow proper change control procedures to assess their impact and formally incorporate them into the project. C. Ignore the new requirements as the current budget and schedule do not allow for any changes: Ignoring mandatory regulatory changes can lead to non-compliance, which could result in penalties, project failure, or reputational damage. D. Proceed with the defined project requirements and delay implementing the new requirements: Delaying the implementation of mandatory changes until after the project execution phase could result in non-compliance and associated risks.

questions.q: A project manager is managing a new development program to automate some technical functions. During project kickoff, the project manager expresses the need for a technical architect to support the project for a moderate amount of time. The project sponsor informs the project manager about an existing technical architect who possesses valuable knowledge but is already assigned at the portfolio level. What engagement model should the project manager use for the technical architect role to ensure project success? *

o.t: Hire a new technical architect who would be solely dedicated to the current project.
Share the existing technical architect so they can be allocated to the current project and other projects.
Hire a new technical architect who would be shared between the current project and other projects.
Assign the existing technical architect to solely be dedicated to the current project.

questions.e: Rationale: Since the technical architect is already working at the portfolio level and possesses valuable knowledge, sharing their time across projects is the most practical solution. This ensures their expertise benefits the current project while maintaining their role at the portfolio level. The project manager should coordinate with the portfolio manager to define a clear allocation of the architect's time and responsibilities. Why not the other options? A. Hire a new technical architect who would be solely dedicated to the current project: Hiring a new architect could take additional time and resources, and the new hire may lack the critical knowledge of the organization's portfolio-level strategies. C. Hire a new technical architect who would be shared between the current project and other projects: Introducing a new hire for shared responsibilities is less effective because the existing architect already possesses valuable institutional knowledge and expertise. D. Assign the existing technical architect to solely be dedicated to the current project: Removing the architect from their portfolio-level responsibilities could disrupt other ongoing initiatives and lead to resource management issues.

questions.q: In a standup meeting, a team member has been providing the same update for five consecutive days. The task which is on the critical path is now at risk for delaying the schedule. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Reassign the task to another member of the team
Support the team member by providing one more resource to complete the task immediately
Ask the team member if there is an impediment and help to remove the blockers
Keep the project sponsor informed about the delay

questions.e: Rationale: In an Agile or hybrid project environment, when a team member provides the same update repeatedly, it signals that there might be an impediment preventing them from making progress. The project manager's role is to identify and remove obstacles so the team can continue to move forward. By addressing the blocker directly, the project manager ensures that the task on the critical path is not delayed further. Why not the other options? A. Reassign the task to another member of the team: Reassigning the task without understanding the root cause may demotivate the team member and not address the actual problem. B. Support the team member by providing one more resource to complete the task immediately: Adding resources may not resolve the underlying issue and could lead to inefficiencies, particularly if the task is not easily divisible. D. Keep the project sponsor informed about the delay: While keeping the sponsor informed is important, it does not address the issue directly. Resolving the problem should take priority before escalating it to the sponsor.

questions.q: A project manager is leading a team of diverse individuals of all ages. The working hours for the project were set at the beginning of the project, and all team members agreed to the hours. However, later in the project, one of the team members informed the project manager that the previously agreed upon hours no longer work due to the team member's personal commitments. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Allow the most senior team members to decide the time that works for the team.
Reassess the team's hours collaboratively so that the team is not impeded by the issue.
Discuss the lack of dedication with the team member and their functional manager.
Remove the team member from the project team to be fair to the other members.

questions.e: Rationale: When a team member's personal commitments change, the project manager should address the issue collaboratively to maintain team cohesion and productivity. By reassessing the working hours with the team, the project manager can explore solutions that work for everyone while ensuring the project is not negatively impacted. This approach demonstrates flexibility and fosters a supportive team environment. Why not the other options? A. Allow the most senior team members to decide the time that works for the team: Delegating this decision to senior members may create bias or unfair outcomes, potentially alienating other team members. C. Discuss the lack of dedication with the team member and their functional manager: Assuming a lack of dedication without first understanding the situation may damage trust and demotivate the team member. D. Remove the team member from the project team to be fair to the other members: Removing the team member without trying to resolve the issue collaboratively is premature and could disrupt the team and project progress.

questions.q: A project manager is assigned to an organizational transformation project. The company typically defines individual performance plans at the beginning of the year, and functional managers conduct feedback reviews at the end of the year. The transformation project team members are concerned that the work they are doing for this project is not aligned with the work included in their individual performance plan for the year. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Meet with the functional managers to align the expected frequency and results reporting for the team members.
Provide performance feedback to the learn members' functional managers at the end of the year.
Assure team members that this project is a high priority for the company and they will be evaluated accordingly.
Request to be made responsible for the performance plans of those on this project team

questions.e: Rationale: Team members’ concerns about their performance plans and reviews must be addressed to avoid disengagement and confusion. By collaborating with functional managers, the project manager can ensure alignment between the transformation project and the employees' individual performance plans. Establishing clear expectations and reporting frequency allows the work on the project to be acknowledged and evaluated as part of the team members’ performance reviews. Why not the other options? B. Provide performance feedback to the team members' functional managers at the end of the year: Waiting until the end of the year does not address the team’s immediate concerns or provide assurance during the project. C. Assure team members that this project is a high priority for the company and they will be evaluated accordingly: Verbal assurances alone are insufficient; formal alignment with the functional managers is needed to ensure that project work is recognized in their performance evaluations. D. Request to be made responsible for the performance plans of those on this project team: The project manager typically does not have authority over team members’ performance plans in a matrix organization. This would require significant organizational restructuring, which is impractical.

questions.q: A team member has a sudden emergency that may last for several days. There are no other team members who can cover their tasks and job duties. What should the project manager do to address this concern? *

o.t: Hold an emergency project team meeting to discuss the situation.
Ask the human resources (HR) manager for an external replacement.
Log the situation in the issue log.
Update the key stakeholders on the issue.

questions.q: A project manager recently finished a project and started managing a new project with a different supervisor. As part of the early project activities, the supervisor from the original project is assigned to the team as a nonsupervisory resource and immediately begins challenging all decisions made by the current supervisor. What should the project manager do to resolve this conflict? *

o.t: Give the project team time to work through the issues with the new supervisor.
Ensure the new supervisor takes the lead when being challenged.
Immediately remove the resource from the project team.
Communicate with the resource on the roles and responsibilities of this project.

questions.e: Rationale: To resolve the conflict, the project manager should clearly communicate the roles and responsibilities of all team members, including the former supervisor. This ensures that everyone understands their position and boundaries within the project. By addressing the issue directly and constructively, the project manager can align the team and prevent further disruptions. Why the others are incorrect: A: Giving the team time to work through the issues may lead to prolonged conflict and disrupt the project’s progress. B: Ensuring the new supervisor takes the lead when challenged may address specific instances but does not resolve the root cause of the behavior. C: Removing the resource immediately is an extreme measure and should be a last resort after attempts to resolve the issue have been made.

questions.q: A project being constructed in a remote rural area is nearing the end of construction. The project manager would like to share the good news with stakeholders. How should the project manager communicate with the local community? *

o.t: Social media
Email
Meetings
Newspapers

questions.e: Rationale: For a remote rural area, meetings are often the most effective way to communicate with the local community. This method allows for face-to-face interaction, fostering trust and engagement while providing an opportunity for the community to ask questions and provide feedback. Meetings are particularly effective in areas where access to technology, such as social media or email, may be limited. Why the others are incorrect: A. Social media: While effective in urban or tech-savvy communities, social media may not reach all members of a remote rural community. B. Email: Many people in rural areas may not have reliable internet access or email accounts, making this method less inclusive. D. Newspapers: While newspapers can help spread the message, they lack the interactive element of meetings, which is important for engaging with the community directly.

questions.q: A company is working on a project to develop an integration of their existing systems. There are known issues in production. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Identify and remove impediments and mitigate the risks.
Ensure the product owner reviews requirements with the team.
Include acceptance criteria in the Definition of Done (DoD).
Review the quality control processes and procedures.

questions.e: Rationale: When there are known issues in production, the project manager’s primary responsibility is to identify and remove impediments that could hinder progress and mitigate risks that might arise from these issues. Addressing these proactively ensures that the project stays on track and that integration challenges do not negatively impact deliverables. Why the others are incorrect: B. Ensure the product owner reviews requirements with the team: While requirement reviews are important, they do not directly address existing production issues or risks related to integration. C. Include acceptance criteria in the Definition of Done (DoD): Having clear acceptance criteria is good practice but does not address the immediate need to handle production issues. D. Review the quality control processes and procedures: While reviewing quality processes is beneficial, it is not the immediate action needed to address existing production issues.

questions.q: A project manager is managing the transition to operations. The project sponsor wants to ensure that good support is provided to the end users. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ensure that the user guide is detailed and has clear instructions.
Ensure that comprehensive documentation is handed over.
Ask the project team to provide operational support for one year.
Ensure that knowledge is transferred to the operations team.

questions.e: Rationale: A successful transition to operations requires effective knowledge transfer to the operations team. This ensures that they are well-prepared to support end users, address issues, and maintain the system. Knowledge transfer includes training, documentation handover, and interactive sessions to clarify responsibilities and processes, ensuring continuity and minimizing disruptions. Why the others are incorrect: A. Ensure that the user guide is detailed and has clear instructions: While a user guide is important, it is only one component of effective knowledge transfer and does not address the full scope of operational support. B. Ensure that comprehensive documentation is handed over: Documentation is critical, but without proper knowledge transfer, the operations team may struggle to understand or apply the information effectively. C. Ask the project team to provide operational support for one year: This is not a sustainable solution, as the project team is typically not responsible for long-term operational support.

questions.q: A healthcare company requires all new employees to attend mandatory computer-based training courses. Because some of the employees work with highly sensitive patient data, the training covers various aspects of data security. In spite of this training, data breaches continue to occur in one of the project teams. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Apply a root-cause analysis on the data breaches.
Ensure that all team members complete the training.
Redesign the training courseware to make it interesting.
Retrain the team members responsible for the breaches.

questions.e: Rationale: To effectively address the issue of data breaches, the project manager should conduct a root-cause analysis to determine why the breaches are occurring despite the mandatory training. This approach allows the project manager to identify underlying issues, such as gaps in the training content, non-compliance, or process weaknesses, and take targeted corrective actions to prevent future breaches. Why the others are incorrect: B. Ensure that all team members complete the training: While ensuring compliance with training requirements is important, it does not address why breaches continue to occur after training. C. Redesign the training courseware to make it interesting: Making training more engaging may improve retention but does not directly address the current breaches or their root causes. D. Retrain the team members responsible for the breaches: Retraining without understanding the root cause might not resolve the issue if the problem lies elsewhere, such as in processes or systems.

questions.q: A project manager is leading three projects in a program focused on starting product commercialization. Once the three projects are launched, the project manager stops attending the recurring team meetings. The program manager asks the project manager to continue attending these meetings to maintain those team touchpoints. This request does not match the project manager's expectation, since a program manager is overseeing the remaining work. How should the project manager approach the situation? *

o.t: Attend only the program meetings where the market launch is being monitored
Provide an answer via email recommending a division of tasks between both roles.
Politely inform the program manager that attending these meetings is no longer required.
Schedule a meeting to discuss the different perspectives and agree on a decision.

questions.e: Rationale: When there is a difference in expectations between the project manager and program manager, the best approach is to schedule a meeting to discuss and align perspectives. This ensures clear communication, mutual understanding of responsibilities, and a collaborative decision on how to proceed, which benefits the program and its objectives. Why the others are incorrect: A. Attend only the program meetings where the market launch is being monitored: This unilateral decision might not align with the program manager's expectations or the needs of the program. B. Provide an answer via email recommending a division of tasks between both roles: Addressing the issue via email lacks the opportunity for a collaborative discussion and may result in misunderstandings. C. Politely inform the program manager that attending these meetings is no longer required: Declining without a discussion may create tension and could negatively impact the program’s success.

questions.q: At a project meeting, a business analyst requires input from a marketing consultant to continue working on a task. The business analyst has tried to contact the consultant but has been told that the consultant does not have the time to discuss the project. What should the project manager do to move the project forward? *

o.t: Escalate the issues about the consultant to the functional manager so the consultant dedicates the necessary time to the project.
Include a new project risk into the risk register and allocate the consultant as the risk owner as it is their responsibility to provide input.
Discuss the request with the consultant and set up time with the business analyst and consultant to discuss the project requirements.
Urge the business analyst to continue contacting the consultant to discuss the project since this is the responsibility of the business analyst.

questions.e: Rationale: The project manager should intervene to facilitate collaboration between the business analyst and the consultant. By discussing the request directly with the consultant and scheduling time for them to work together, the project manager ensures that the necessary input is provided, enabling the task to progress without further delays. Why the others are incorrect: A: Escalating the issue to the functional manager may be necessary if the consultant remains uncooperative, but it should not be the first step as it might damage relationships and delay resolution. B: Adding a risk to the risk register highlights the issue but does not address the immediate need for the consultant’s input to move the task forward. D: Urging the business analyst to continue contacting the consultant does not resolve the roadblock, as the consultant has already expressed a lack of availability.

questions.q: While finalizing project management plans, a customer provides the project manager with a new set of quality standards to which the final product must adhere. What should the project manager do to ensure a smooth delivery of the product? *

o.t: Involve the client in risk identification.
Agree with the client on acceptance criteria.
Involve the client in a performance gap analysis.
Agree with the client on a new project charter.

questions.e: Rationale: Agreeing on the acceptance criteria ensures that the project’s final product meets the newly provided quality standards. This step clearly defines the specific benchmarks that the product must achieve for the customer to consider it acceptable, ensuring alignment and a smoother delivery process. Why the others are incorrect: A. Involve the client in risk identification: While involving the client in risk identification is important, it does not directly address the need to meet the new quality standards. C. Involve the client in a performance gap analysis: A gap analysis identifies differences between current performance and desired outcomes, but it does not establish the criteria needed for product acceptance. D. Agree with the client on a new project charter: Updating the project charter is unnecessary in this scenario, as the acceptance criteria can be addressed within the project’s quality or scope management processes.

questions.q: A project manager working on a large-scale network implementation is frustrated with the hardware supplier. Their deliveries have been consistently late and frequently do not have vital components. The project manager's company has decided to cancel the contract and move to a new supplier, but the only other option is an overseas company. What should the project manager do first to proceed with this change? *

o.t: Engage the services of an interpreter who understands the project domain.
Check social media to determine if there are any common connections that use the new supplier.
Request assistance from the procurement department on the next steps.
Become aware of any cultural characteristics of the new supplier that could impact negotiation.

questions.e: Rationale: The procurement department has the expertise to handle supplier transitions, including contract negotiations, compliance with company policies, and evaluating the terms of the new supplier relationship. Engaging with the procurement department ensures that the process of switching suppliers is conducted efficiently and aligns with organizational protocols. Why the others are incorrect: A. Engage the services of an interpreter who understands the project domain: While this might be helpful later in communication with an overseas supplier, it is not the first step in managing the supplier transition. B. Check social media to determine if there are any common connections that use the new supplier: This step might provide informal insights but is not a formal or reliable way to manage supplier relationships. D. Become aware of any cultural characteristics of the new supplier that could impact negotiation: Understanding cultural characteristics is important but should occur after the procurement department initiates the transition process.

questions.q: A hybrid project has just been deployed, and the project manager is planning project closure with lessons learned workshops. A key stakeholder informs the project manager that having the Scrum team in the workshops is a waste of time because the project was delivered successfully. What should the project manager do? *

o.t: Ask the Scrum team members to share retrospectives.
Ask the scrum master to attend the workshops.
Invite the Scrum team members as optional participants.
Invite the Scrum team members as mandatory participants.

questions.e: Rationale: Even if the project was delivered successfully, lessons learned workshops are a critical part of the project closure process to capture insights, identify areas for improvement, and document best practices for future projects. Including the Scrum team members as mandatory participants ensures their perspectives and experiences are captured, as they directly contributed to the project execution and can provide valuable insights. Why the others are incorrect: A. Ask the Scrum team members to share retrospectives: While retrospectives are useful, they are specific to sprints. Lessons learned workshops have a broader scope and should formally include the Scrum team. B. Ask the scrum master to attend the workshops: Involving the Scrum master alone is insufficient because the entire Scrum team can provide diverse and valuable feedback. C. Invite the Scrum team members as optional participants: Making participation optional risks missing critical input from team members who played an active role in project delivery.

questions.q: A project team member wants to select specific challenging tasks in the subsequent iteration. How can the project lead help the team member in the next iteration? *

o.t: Assign the challenging tasks to the team member.
